title: Remote Workers Lose 58 Minutes of Movement a Day
paragraphs: Working from home has many benefits. You do not need to travel to work, and you have more free time. But a new study shows that people move a lot less on the days they work at home.
The study was done by researchers at the University of Turku in Finland. It was published in 2026 in the International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity.

The researchers studied 97 university workers. These people worked some days at the office and some days at home. For seven days, each person wore a small sensor on their leg. The sensor measured how much time they spent sitting, standing, walking and doing exercise.

The researchers then compared each person's office days with their home days. On home days, people sat for about 44 minutes more. They also did about 58 fewer minutes of light and harder physical activity, like walking. However, they spent about 14 more minutes in bed.

The biggest change was for people who usually walked or rode a bike to work. On home days, they lost the exercise from their trip to the office. Their sitting time outside work hours went up by about 30 minutes.
The study had some limits. Most of the people were women, and they all worked at one university. Also, the study did not measure people's health directly.

Still, the results are important for people who work from home. Sitting too much is bad for health. So, on home days, it may be a good idea to take short walks, stand up more often, or find another way to stay active.
